articles.desc: Reacting to the Supreme Court order, Suresh said the government would have to comply with the court's directions but was considering framing regulations and imposing restrictions rather than imposing a blanket ban on bike taxis.

articles.title: US Treasury yields drop for day and week; AI trade concern spurs safe-haven bid
articles.desc: US Treasury yields experienced a significant decline due to heightened investor concerns surrounding the AI trade. As a result, investors shifted their focus towards safe-haven assets such as Treasury securities. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note fell below 5% for the first time in several months. Concerns about rising company debt and spending related to AI contributed to investor unease in recent weeks.

articles.title: Dollar weaker as Fed-fueled rally stalls; lower US yields help yen
articles.desc: The US dollar has encountered a modest downturn, sliding to 103.86 as investor confidence wavers in the currency market. Despite this pullback, traders expect the Federal Reserve to maintain a hawkish stance in upcoming statements. Concurrently, Bitcoin has dipped below the $60,000 mark, sparking concerns about its valuation amidst ongoing market volatility.

articles.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
articles.desc: Levent Alpoge, a member of the company's technical staff, made the announcement Friday by way of a four-page explanation posted on his website. He said that he believes by working with Claude, he has found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.

articles.title: Crude prices may normalise to USD 70 by end-2027 as global oil market moves into surplus: Report
articles.desc: Global crude oil prices are projected to normalize around USD 70 per barrel by the end of 2027. Rising non-OPEC+ supplies and declining Chinese oil demand are expected to lead to a market surplus. Refining margins are likely to remain elevated in the near term before gradual normalization occurs. Geopolitical tensions, particularly between the US and Iran, are likely to influence oil supply dynamics.

articles.title: Gold's slide deepens as AI rout, rate-hike bets hurt bullion
articles.desc: Gold prices plummeted by 3% on Friday, settling at a 14-month low of $3,502.49 per ounce. This sharp decline is largely due to a hawkish interest rate forecast and a significant selloff within AI stocks. Analysts point to forced liquidations of gold holdings as a factor, alongside increasing expectations of US borrowing costs, contributing to the commodity's bearish trend this week.

articles.title: UK stocks sink as global selloff weighs on banks and miners
articles.desc: UK stocks experienced significant declines on Friday, resulting from a global market selloff linked to AI valuations. The FTSE 100 index closed at a five-month low, influenced by sharp declines in banking and mining stocks. Despite stronger-than-expected UK retail sales, declines in sectors outweighed positive news. Defensive consumer companies offered some support amid broader financial concerns.

articles.title: European shares post worst week in over a year as AI trade unravels
articles.desc: European shares declined sharply, reflecting deeper worries about the sustainability of AI-related investments and overall economic growth. Concerns intensified after Anthropic's initial public offering did not restore confidence in the tech sector. The overall market decline affected various sectors, including cyclical stocks and semiconductor companies, due to profit-taking by investors. Despite recent losses, the STOXX 600 index remains up year-to-date, surpassing the performance of the S&P 500.

articles.title: Tech leads global stocks rout, Treasury yields fall
articles.desc: On Friday, global stock markets faced a harsh sell-off, notably impacting technology stocks. In response, US traders turned to safer investments as the 10-year yield sharply decreased. The Dow Jones Industrial Average took a major hit, alongside declines in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. However, consumer staples emerged relatively unscathed within the S&P 500.

articles.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: 'Black Friday' brings consumer spending into focus for AI-rocked market
articles.desc: As the holiday season draws near, investors are keenly watching consumer spending patterns amid rising inflation fears. With US retail sales expected to show a modest uptick, this hints at consumer strength. Major retailers express optimism about this year's holiday shopping, although high gasoline and energy costs may pose challenges for spending. Investors are analyzing economic signals to understand potential market effects in the upcoming week.

articles.title: Sebi proposes limiting tenure of chief executives, independent directors of stock exchanges, market infrastruction institutions
articles.desc: India's Securities and Exchange Board is proposing crucial adjustments to governance norms affecting market institutions. Key suggestions include lowering the age threshold for public interest directors from 75 to 70 years, instituting a maximum of two three-year terms for directors, and restricting managing directors to an eight-year tenure. Current executives can finish their ongoing terms despite these proposed changes. SEBI is seeking public feedback on these recommendations by December 11.

articles.title: No FAST-DS declaration needed for foreign bank a/c up to Rs 20 lakh with disclosed funds: I-T dept
articles.desc: The Income Tax Department has announced exemptions for individuals with foreign bank accounts under FAST-DS. Individuals with balances up to Rs 20 lakh from disclosed sources do not need to file declarations. This exemption applies as long as the accounts contain no undisclosed income or unaccounted deposits. The scheme provides a one-time opportunity to disclose foreign assets and income by December 31.

Rupee climbs past 93/USD as investors seek shelter in Indian stocks, shorts unwind
articles.desc: The Indian rupee has strengthened past the 93-per-dollar mark for the first time since April. This recovery is attributed to over $12 billion of foreign investments in Indian equities in November. Hedge funds have unwound bearish positions on the rupee, contributing to its recent gains. The Reserve Bank of India has taken measures to support the local currency amidst stabilization efforts.

articles.title: RBI expected to raise rates in December, deliver final hike in February: Report
articles.desc: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to raise its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December and take it to 6% in February as inflation breaches its 6% tolerance limit, a Reuters poll showed. Rising energy costs and uneven monsoon rainfall have intensified inflationary pressures.

articles.title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
articles.desc: People stocking up on long-life food drove retail sales higher October, according to official data.

articles.title: India's capital goods market could reach $1.2 trillion by 2047, driven by data centres, chips: Report
articles.desc: India's capital goods market could expand to USD 1-1.2 trillion by 2047, driven by rising investments in data centres, semiconductors, defence and clean energy, a CII-BCG report said. Annual capital expenditure across major industries is projected to rise 30% to Rs 32 lakh crore by FY27-29.

articles.title: Anthropic's debut rally fades as shares crack 7% in US pre-market trade
articles.desc: Anthropic shares fell as much as 7.4% in premarket trading on their second day, as a global market selloff and concerns over the AI trade overshadowed the optimism surrounding its record-setting IPO debut. After surging 39% from the IPO price on Thursday, the stock ended 17% higher. A steep valuation and competitive threats added to investor caution.

articles.title: Sharp rupee appreciation may cut IT firms' FY27 earnings by up to 13%: Report
articles.desc: According to a new report, the appreciation of the Indian rupee could lead Indian IT companies to experience reduced earnings. The stronger rupee against foreign currencies may significantly impact profitability, especially for firms with substantial European exposure. As traditional cost-saving strategies grow scarce, maintaining margins will be a challenge, compounded by the current economic environment affecting pricing strategies in the industry.
